name: BadmintonQA
description: Understanding a full sports match requires reasoning about how patterns of play, match dynamics, and competitors’ behaviors evolve over time. Video question answering (QA) offers a natural way to evaluate such understanding. However, existing sports QA datasets mainly use short, isolated video clips and therefore focus on temporally localized actions and events rather than match-level reasoning. In this study, we introduce BadmintonQA, a long-video question answering dataset for full-match badminton understanding. BadmintonQA contains 533 four-choice questions over 19 full matches, including 12 men’s-singles and 7 men’s-doubles matches from four BWF World Tour tournaments. We further propose EviCover, a training-free and backbone-agnostic frame selector that first divides a video into temporal segments, then selects those most useful for distinguishing the answer options based on their captions, and finally retrieves one question-relevant frame from each selected segment. Experiments on BadmintonQA and LVBench demonstrate the effectiveness of EviCover across sports-specific and general long-video question answering settings. Our dataset and code are publicly available at https://github.com/Ning-D/BadmintonQA
